option_name: Anaerobic digestion of slaughterhouse by-products and paunch waste
duty: Biogas from blood, gut contents, sludges and low-risk ABP fractions to fuel site boilers/CHP
trl_basis: No formal TRL; peer-reviewed studies of slaughterhouse by-product AD and operating plants in Europe; AHDB guidance for livestock waste AD
key_constraints: Animal by-product regulations (pasteurisation/Cat 2-3 handling); ammonia inhibition of digesters; feedstock competes with rendering
uk_status: Commercial technology; UK deployment site-specific, often via off-site AD/rendering rather than on-site plants
provenance: [SD_SLAUGHTER_AD] Peer-reviewed work on AD of slaughterhouse by-products; AHDB AD guidance

option_name: Full use of biogas CHP jacket/exhaust heat for digester heating and pasteurisation
duty: Parasitic heat loads (digester ~40C, pasteurisation ~70C) met from own CHP heat
trl_basis: Standard practice at UK AD plants; ADBA documents CHP heat use incl. 50-70C digestate evaporation at Barkip
key_constraints: Only applies where CHP retained; heat availability varies with engine load; competes with heat export revenue
uk_status: Widely deployed; ADBA estimates 135MWth of CHP heat still wasted UK-wide
provenance: [REF_ADBA_HEAT] ADBA sector guidance on using biogas CHP heat

option_name: Heat pumps for digester heating and pasteurisation (freeing biogas for upgrading)
duty: Electric heat pumps supply 40-70C digester/pasteuriser heat instead of burning biogas
trl_basis: No published TRL located; techno-economic/modelling assessment stage for this duty (Bioresource Technology, 2022); component heat pumps are TRL 9
key_constraints: Low-grade heat source needed for good COP (digestate, effluent); interacts with upgrading economics; grid capacity
uk_status: Studied; not standard practice at UK AD sites
provenance: [REF_BITE22] Peer-reviewed assessment of AD + heat pump integration

option_name: High-temperature air-to-air heat pumps replacing gas warm-air heaters
duty: Direct replacement of gas-fired warm-air unit heaters in high-bay workshops and warehouses with air-to-air heat pump units (no wet distribution system)
trl_basis: Air-to-air heat pump / VRF equipment is fully commercial worldwide; DESNZ/ERM rates heat pumps generally TRL 7-9
key_constraints: Discharge air temperature lower than gas warm-air heaters so more units/airflow needed; high-bay mounting and stratification management; refrigerant charge (F-gas) limits on large splits; electrical capacity
uk_status: Commercial products available; less common than air-to-water in UK industrial retrofit practice
provenance: [REF_UKBCH_ASHP] UK Business Climate Hub covers air-source heat pumps including air-to-air units for business buildings

option_name: Alkali-activated / geopolymer cement-free binders (e.g. Cemfree)
duty: Replace Portland cement entirely with alkali-activated GGBS/PFA binder systems
trl_basis: No numeric TRL located; reviews describe industrially available production technologies; niche commercial UK use
key_constraints: Activator cost/supply; reliance on constrained GGBS/PFA; no harmonised EN design standard (PAS 8820 route); durability track record; supplier fragility (Cemfree parent DB Group entered administration 2024)
uk_status: Niche commercial: Cemfree used by Network Rail, Environment Agency and others
provenance: [R_AAM] Heliyon 2023 review of alkali-activated cement production technologies; ICE Network Rail Cemfree case (R_CEMFREE)

option_name: Ammonia as a direct combustion fuel for industry
duty: Boiler/furnace fuel or co-firing; hydrogen carrier for sites without pipeline H2
trl_basis: No published numeric TRL for industrial process heat located. Alnajideen et al. (2024, Carbon Neutrality) review notes barriers 'to overcome before reaching full commercial maturity' (NOx, flame stability, materials); single-fuel burner tests reported by OEMs (e.g. MHI, 2023)
key_constraints: N2O/NOx and ammonia slip; low flame speed needs burner redesign; toxicity, storage and permitting; ammonia supply chain; energy penalty vs direct H2
uk_status: None for process heat; research stage
provenance: [ALNAJIDEEN2024] Review-wide maturity statements; no TRL assigned by source, hence null

option_name: Air-source heat pump space heating for industrial buildings
duty: Space heating of factories, workshops and depots via air-to-water heat pumps serving AHU coils, fan convectors or radiant panels
trl_basis: Mature mass-market technology; DESNZ/ERM 'Future Opportunities for Electrification' rates industrial heat pumps TRL 7-9, with sub-100C space-heat duties at the top of the range
key_constraints: Electrical supply capacity; external plant space; lower flow temperatures require larger emitters or AHU coil changes; poor building fabric inflates capacity and cost; COP falls at design outdoor conditions
uk_status: Commercial; active UK supplier base and government-backed SME guidance (UK Business Climate Hub); uptake limited by capex and electricity/gas price ratio
provenance: [REF_UKBCH_ASHP] UK Business Climate Hub guidance on ASHPs for business premises

option_name: Battery-electric mobile plant / non-road mobile machinery
duty: Motive power for forklifts, loaders, excavators, telehandlers, yard vehicles; best for low/medium-power duty cycles
trl_basis: ERM techno-economic feasibility study for DESNZ (2023) holds TRLs in Appendix 9.8 (not extractable in this review) and rates battery electric 'commercially available' for multiple archetypes; DESNZ CfE summary (2025) records respondents arguing 'electric machinery should be higher [TRL], mostly for low to medium archetypes'
key_constraints: Site charging infrastructure and grid connection; duty-cycle/shift length ('not capable of doing a full day's work on a single charge yet' for some archetypes); capex premium; cold/heavy duty limits
uk_status: Deployed for small machinery (electric forklifts mainstream); demonstration for heavy plant
provenance: [ERM_NRMM2023] Availability matrix Table 4; numeric TRLs exist in Appendix 9.8 but could not be extracted - flagged in challenges

option_name: Biochar/charcoal injection in blast furnace (Bio-PCI)
duty: Substituting biogenic char for pulverised injection coal at BF tuyeres
trl_basis: Commercially practised in Brazilian charcoal mini blast furnaces; partial substitution in large BFs assessed at pilot/trial scale (Bio-PCI techno-economic literature)
key_constraints: Sustainable biomass availability at scale; char mechanical/combustion properties; ~40-50% PCI substitution ceiling in large BFs
uk_status: No UK trials reported; declining relevance with BF closures
provenance: [REF_BIOPCI] Peer-reviewed study of charcoal injection (Bio-PCI) CO2 reduction potential and economics

option_name: Hydrogen injection into blast furnace tuyeres
duty: Partial replacement of PCI coal with hydrogen injected at BF tuyeres, cutting CO2 up to ~20% at full deployment
trl_basis: thyssenkrupp Duisburg BF9 single-tuyere trials (2019-2021, first test phase concluded); H2Stahl project scaling to full tuyere set — demonstration stage, not commercial
key_constraints: Coke still required for burden support; limited abatement ceiling (~20%); hydrogen supply and cost; burner/tuyere modifications
uk_status: UK relevance closing as Port Talbot BFs shut (2024) and Scunthorpe transitions; option only relevant while BFs continue operating
provenance: [REF_TKH2] thyssenkrupp Steel press release on completed first hydrogen injection test phase

option_name: Bio-feedstock co-processing in refinery units
duty: Co-processing biogenic feedstocks (e.g. used cooking oil) in hydrotreaters/FCC for renewable fuels
trl_basis: Commercial at Phillips 66 Humber refinery since 2018 (first UK SAF/renewable diesel production by co-processing)
key_constraints: Feedstock availability and cost; catalyst/metallurgy limits on blend ratio; benefit mainly lifecycle/scope 3
uk_status: Commercial at Humber refinery
provenance: [p66_renewables] Phillips 66 UK renewable fuels programme at Humber

option_name: Biocarbon substitution for coke/coal in sinter, EAF and cupola
duty: Biochar/biocoke replacing fossil carbon as sinter-plant solid fuel, EAF charge/injection carbon and foundry cupola coke
trl_basis: Review evidence (Fuel, 2023) of pilot and industrial trials of biochar in sintering, EAF slag foaming/charge carbon and cokemaking blends; not yet standard practice
key_constraints: Char reactivity, strength and ash chemistry differ from coke; supply chain immature; cost premium
uk_status: Identified in UK/EU steel and foundry decarbonisation literature; limited UK trials
provenance: [REF_BIOCHAR_REV] Review: 'To what extent could biochar replace coal and coke in steel industries?'

option_name: Biogas upgrading to biomethane for grid injection (in place of onsite CHP)
duty: Site output shifted from electricity+heat to biomethane export; parasitic heat re-provided by heat pumps/boilers
trl_basis: Membrane/water-wash upgrading commercially deployed at UK AD plants (ADBA sector material)
key_constraints: Gas grid proximity and entry costs; loses free CHP heat so parasitic heating must be re-provided; policy-dependent (GGSS) economics
uk_status: Commercial and growing under Green Gas Support Scheme
provenance: [REF_ADBA_HEAT] ADBA biogas-use guidance; upgrading vs CHP trade-off is sector-standard, note ref is general ADBA material

option_name: Biomass boilers (solid biomass steam/hot water)
duty: Steam and hot water to conventional boiler conditions; baseload site heat
trl_basis: CCC/Element Energy assumptions log (2019): 'Biomass Steam Boiler 2018' in the 'Date when TRL 9 achieved' rollout table (i.e. TRL 9 since before 2018); Element Energy/Jacobs for BEIS (2018) classify biomass boilers as 'already commercially available'
key_constraints: Sustainable feedstock supply and price; fuel storage/handling space; air-quality permitting (PM/NOx); CCC cautions on best-use of finite biomass
uk_status: Deployed at many UK sites (RHI legacy)
provenance: [CCC_LOG2019] Rollout table p11; EE_JACOBS2018 maturity classification

option_name: Biomethane (grid-injected or onsite AD) as natural gas substitute
duty: Drop-in for any natural-gas duty (boilers, kilns, CHP) with no equipment change
trl_basis: DESNZ/DfT NRMM CfE summary of responses (2025) records that 'biomethane is already at a TRL level of 8+'; anaerobic digestion and upgrading operate commercially at scale in the UK (grid injection)
key_constraints: Feedstock availability caps volumes; certificate/market cost premium; competition with other biomethane uses; onsite AD needs feedstock logistics and space
uk_status: Deployed - 100+ UK grid-injection plants; used via green gas certificates
provenance: [DESNZ_NRMM_CFE2025] Respondent-evidence TRL statement (vehicle-fuel context) - weakest of the numeric TRLs used; see challenges

option_name: Building fabric upgrade (insulation, air-tightness, doors)
duty: Roof and wall insulation, air-tightness, rapid-action doors and glazing improvements to reduce space-heat demand and enable smaller low-carbon heating plant
trl_basis: No published TRL; mature construction practice
key_constraints: Disruption and roof access; marginal economics on short remaining building life or leased premises (landlord-tenant split incentive)
uk_status: Fully commercial; Carbon Trust estimates up to 15% total energy bill savings from fabric measures
provenance: [REF_CT_FABRIC] Carbon Trust Building Fabric guide covers insulation and air-tightness measures for industrial buildings

option_name: Limestone calcined clay cement (LC3)
duty: Ternary clinker-calcined clay-limestone cement cutting CO2 up to ~40% vs OPC
trl_basis: No numeric TRL located; peer-reviewed reviews describe progression from lab to industrial application with commercial production in several countries
key_constraints: Requires suitable kaolinitic clay and clay calciner investment (~800C heat, itself needing decarbonisation); colour acceptance; UK standards adoption; no UK production line yet
uk_status: Not yet produced in UK; standards routes emerging
provenance: [R_LC3_REV] Heliyon 2024 comprehensive LC3 review; LC3 project site (R_LC3) reports ~40 companies in 25 countries engaged and up to 40% CO2 reduction

option_name: Calcium looping CO2 capture
duty: High-temperature CaO/CaCO3 looping capture, well suited to cement/lime flue gas with heat recovery
trl_basis: IEA CCUS in Clean Energy Transitions (2020): calcium looping 'currently at TRL 5-6, have been tested, mostly at the pilot plant scale'; Islam & Patlolla (2025): CaL 'advanced rapidly to TRL 6-7 and has been tested in several pilot plants'
key_constraints: CO2 T&S dependence; oxy-fired calciner adds ASU; sorbent degradation; major process integration/rebuild; pilot scale only
uk_status: None; EU pilots (e.g. CLEANKER)
provenance: [IEA_CCUS2020] IEA gives 5-6; ISLAM2025 gives 6-7 - range spans both, per instruction on disagreement

option_name: Carbonated manufactured aggregate (accelerated carbonation of residues, e.g. O.C.O Technology)
duty: Manufactured limestone aggregate from APCr + CO2 used in building blocks
trl_basis: Commercial UK operation: O.C.O (ex-Carbon8) operates UK plants and has treated >500,000 t of APCr; product used in block manufacture
key_constraints: Feedstock (air pollution control residues) availability and plant siting; block-spec approvals; CO2 sourcing
uk_status: Commercial in UK; aggregate supplied to UK blockmakers
provenance: [R_OCO] O.C.O Technology pages; UKGBC solution listing (R_UKGBC) for manufactured limestone aggregate

option_name: CO2 (carbonation) curing of precast concrete and blocks
duty: Cure unreinforced precast products in CO2-rich chambers, sequestering CO2 and replacing steam/heat curing
trl_basis: No numeric TRL located; peer-reviewed industrial demonstration study of CO2 mineralisation curing published (2022)
key_constraints: Sealed curing chambers and CO2 supply; standards acceptance; best for unreinforced products (carbonation lowers pH, unsuitable for reinforced elements); cycle time management
uk_status: Not deployed at scale in UK; demonstrations overseas
provenance: [R_CO2CURE] Industrial demonstration study on CO2 mineralization curing for concrete (PMC)

option_name: Carbothermic reduction of alumina
duty: Direct carbothermic smelting of alumina to aluminium at ~2000C+, potentially lower capex/energy than electrolysis
trl_basis: Alcoa-Elkem advanced reactor process reached laboratory/small-pilot stage and was discontinued; reviews class all carbothermic concepts as experimental
key_constraints: Aluminium carbide formation and low yields; extreme temperatures; emits CO2 unless with capture; development largely abandoned
uk_status: No UK activity; speculative
provenance: [REF_CARBOTHERMIC] Peer-reviewed review of alternative Al production methods (Rhamdhani et al., Mineral Processing and Extractive Metallurgy, 2013)

option_name: Clinker substitution / multi-component cements (GGBS, PFA, limestone fines, CEM II/VI)
duty: Reduce clinker factor of cement and of concrete mixes by substituting clinker with SCMs and limestone fines
trl_basis: Commercially deployed; MPA UK Concrete roadmap identifies clinker substitution and low-carbon multi-component cements as a core deployed/near-term lever
key_constraints: UK GGBS and PFA supply declining (blast furnace closures, coal phase-out); standards limits (BS 8500, updated 2023 to allow multi-component cements); performance/early-strength trade-offs
uk_status: Commercial and widespread; BS 8500:2023 broadened permitted cement types
provenance: [R_MPA_ROADMAP] MPA UK Concrete Roadmap to Beyond Net Zero quantifies decarbonised electricity/fuel switching and low-carbon cements incl. clinker substitution

option_name: CO2 mineralisation in fresh concrete (CO2 injection at batching, e.g. CarbonCure)
duty: Inject CO2 into fresh mix to mineralise as CaCO3, enabling cement content reduction
trl_basis: No numeric TRL located; commercially deployed at hundreds of ready-mix plants (mainly North America) per vendor and reviews
key_constraints: Small abatement per m3 (~3-6% via cement reduction); CO2 supply logistics; mix design approvals; limited UK adoption to date
uk_status: Early/limited UK adoption; commercial overseas
provenance: [R_CARBONCURE] CarbonCure carbon mineralization in concrete technical page

option_name: Coke oven gas hydrogen recovery/valorisation
duty: Separation of the ~55-60% hydrogen fraction of coke oven gas (PSA/membranes) for use as low-carbon-intensity fuel or feedstock
trl_basis: PSA hydrogen recovery from COG is commercially established (peer-reviewed comparative analysis, Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 2021)
key_constraints: Gas cleaning (tar, sulphur, BTX) upstream; displaces COG from underfiring which must be substituted; economics site-specific
uk_status: Not deployed at UK coke plants
provenance: [REF_COG_H2] ACS I&ECR review of technical alternatives for hydrogen recovery from coke oven gas

option_name: Coke dry quenching with waste-heat power recovery
displaces: grid electricity; coke oven gas (steam raising)
duty: Quenching hot coke with inert gas and recovering sensible heat to steam/power (~85-95 kWh electricity per tonne coke)
trl_basis: CDQ is commercially deployed at large scale, especially in Japan and China (CTCN technology description; Nippon Steel Engineering reference plants)
key_constraints: High capital cost; suits larger batteries; retrofit space; remaining UK coke plants small and ageing
uk_status: Not installed at UK coke plants
provenance: [REF_CDQ] Climate Technology Centre & Network description of coke dry quenching for the iron and steel sector

option_name: Compressed air system optimisation (leaks, pressure, heat recovery)
duty: Reduces compressor electricity; compressor heat recovery can serve <80C heat
trl_basis: No published TRL located; standard commercial practice, outside TRL frameworks in the sources reviewed
key_constraints: Persistence of savings requires ongoing management; none technical
uk_status: Deployed; routinely identified in UK site audits
provenance: [HASANBEIGI2021] TRL null per rules; context reference only

option_name: Advanced controls, energy management and variable speed drives
duty: 5-15%-class savings on motors, fans, pumps and process control across all utilities
trl_basis: No published TRL located; VSDs and control systems are ubiquitous commercial products not covered by TRL frameworks in the sources reviewed
key_constraints: None material - payback and management attention; interacts with all other options (do-first measure)
uk_status: Deployed universally but under-adopted
provenance: [HASANBEIGI2021] TRL null per rules; reference for general electrification/efficiency context only

option_name: Cupola-to-induction furnace conversion in foundries
duty: Replacing coke-fired cupola (or gas-fired) melting with mains-frequency/medium-frequency electric induction melting
trl_basis: Documented commercial conversions (e.g. foundry-planet case study); induction melting is standard commercial technology
key_constraints: Large grid connection/power demand; loses cupola's tolerance of dirty/cheap charge; batch vs continuous melting; capital cost
uk_status: Cast Metals Federation Net Zero roadmap identifies electrification of melting as the core decarbonisation route for UK foundries
provenance: [REF_FP_CUPOLA] Foundry-planet case study of a successful cupola-to-induction conversion; CMF roadmap (REF_CMF) for UK context

option_name: RO/NF membrane pre-concentration before evaporation
duty: Reverse osmosis/nanofiltration to remove water from milk/whey at low temperature ahead of evaporators and spray dryers
trl_basis: No formal TRL; peer-reviewed dairy processing reviews describe RO concentration as commercially applied in dairy processing
key_constraints: Fouling and cleaning chemical load; achievable solids limited (~18-30%) so evaporation still needed; product functionality effects
uk_status: Commercially available; applied at dairy sites internationally and in UK whey processing
provenance: [RO_DAIRY] Peer-reviewed review of reverse osmosis applications in dairy processing (concentration prior to evaporation/drying)

option_name: Destratification fans and conversion to zoned radiant heating
duty: Cut space-heat demand in tall spaces: destratification fans return roof-level warm air to floor level; conversion from warm-air to zoned radiant heating heats occupants/surfaces rather than the full air volume
trl_basis: No published TRL located; long-established commercial measure recommended in Carbon Trust HVAC guidance
key_constraints: Benefit depends on building height and heater type; radiant conversion needs gas or electric radiant emitters and re-zoning; residual fossil use if gas radiant retained
uk_status: Fully commercial; standard energy-survey recommendation for UK sheds and workshops
provenance: [REF_CT_HVAC] Carbon Trust HVAC guide (CTV046) covers destratification and radiant heating for tall industrial spaces; see also Carbon Charter destratification datasheet

option_name: Diesel-electric hybrid drive mobile crushing/screening plant
duty: Interim efficiency step: electric drivetrains powered by onboard genset, switchable to grid
trl_basis: Commercial products; OEM-claimed up to 25% fuel reduction (Hub-4, 2026)
key_constraints: Still fossil-fuelled unless grid-connected or run on HVO; partial abatement only
uk_status: Commercially available and in service in UK
provenance: [REF_HUB4_2026] Same source documents hybrid e-drive plant as bridge to full electric

option_name: Digestate drying/concentration using CHP waste heat
duty: Dry digestate fibre or evaporate liquor (50-70C) with recovered engine heat, cutting digestate haulage and fossil drying fuel
trl_basis: Commercial systems operating (ADBA Barkip case study: CHP-heated vacuum evaporators at 50-70C; Stronga FlowDrya product line)
key_constraints: Only where CHP heat surplus exists; dryer capex; ammonia emissions/odour control from drying
uk_status: Commercially deployed at UK AD plants
provenance: [REF_ADBA_HEAT] ADBA documents CHP-heat digestate concentration; FlowDrya is a UK commercial digestate dryer

option_name: Direct separation calcination (LEILAC-type) for process CO2
duty: Indirectly heated calciner capturing near-pure CO2 from limestone calcination (cement/lime process emissions only)
trl_basis: IEA CCUS in Clean Energy Transitions (2020): direct separation of cement process emissions rated 'TRL 6'; LEILAC-1 pilot (Lixhe) demonstrated CO2 separation at 95% purity per LEILAC Roadmap (2021), which does not itself state TRL numbers
key_constraints: Captures process CO2 only (fuel CO2 needs separate measure or electric/H2 heating); calciner replacement; CO2 T&S dependence; scale-up via LEILAC-2 class demos
uk_status: None in UK; pilot (Belgium) and demonstration (Germany) under LEILAC projects
provenance: [IEA_CCUS2020] TRL 6 quote; LEILAC2021 for project status

option_name: Anaerobic digestion of pot ale, draff and spent wash for biogas
duty: On/near-site biogas from distillery co-products to fuel boilers or upgrade to biomethane
trl_basis: SWA/Ricardo net-zero pathway describes AD as 'relatively mature technology which is already in use in the whisky sector'; no numeric TRL published
key_constraints: Competes with animal-feed value of draff/pot ale syrup; seasonal/variable feedstock; digestate management; copper in pot ale
uk_status: Operational at multiple Scottish sites (e.g. Glenfiddich, Dufftown cluster); assessed for nine operational distilleries in peer-reviewed study
provenance: [AD_NINE_DIST] Peer-reviewed assessment of AD potential at nine operational distilleries; SWA pathway rates AD mature and deployed

option_name: Dry-route body preparation (dry milling/granulation replacing wet slip and spray drying)
duty: Eliminate spray-dryer thermal demand in ceramic body preparation
trl_basis: No TRL located; peer-reviewed comparison of dry vs wet route shows large energy/water savings; industrially used in some overseas tile production
key_constraints: Product quality (pressing behaviour, surface finish); mainly applicable where spray drying/wet routes used (tiles, some tableware); reformulation required
uk_status: Not identified in UK production
provenance: [R_DRYROUTE] Journal of Cleaner Production 2017 dry vs wet route study for ceramic tile body preparation

option_name: EAF scrap preheating (Consteel/shaft/tunnel systems)
duty: Continuous or shaft preheating of scrap using EAF off-gas heat, cutting EAF electricity use ~50-100 kWh/t
trl_basis: Consteel and shaft-furnace preheating commercially installed at dozens of EAF plants worldwide (IspatGuru technical review)
key_constraints: Retrofit space and layout; dioxin/VOC control in preheater off-gas; scrap quality effects
uk_status: Applicable to new UK EAFs (Port Talbot, Scunthorpe) and existing UK EAF plants
provenance: [REF_CONSTEEL] IspatGuru technical article on the Consteel EAF process and its energy savings

option_name: Electron-beam cured coatings
duty: Low-energy electron-beam curing of coatings (demonstrated for automotive interior plastic parts), eliminating thermal cure ovens
trl_basis: UV+EB Technology (2016) documents development of low-energy EB for automotive interior plastic coatings; no formal TRL published
key_constraints: Shielding and capital cost; line-speed/geometry limits; chemistry requalification; supplier ecosystem immature for automotive
uk_status: Not deployed in UK automotive plants; EB curing commercial only in printing/converting niches
provenance: [REF_UVEB_EB] Trade-journal account of low-energy EB curing development for automotive interior plastics

option_name: Electric infrared heating/drying
duty: Surface heating, drying and curing of coatings, paper, textiles, food; typically <500C surface duties
trl_basis: No published numeric TRL located. Hasanbeigi et al. (2021, Electrifying U.S. Industry) list infrared among commercially available electrotechnologies ('high overall efficiency, faster response time than gas convection systems')
key_constraints: Suits surface/thin-web duties, not bulk heating; product-specific validation; grid capacity minor (modular units)
uk_status: Deployed commercially in coating/curing lines
provenance: [HASANBEIGI2021] Electrotechnology descriptions; commercial-availability statement only, no TRL number - flagged in challenges

option_name: Electric calcination / electric kilns (incl. rotodynamic heaters)
duty: High-temperature kiln/calciner duties ~900-1450C (lime, cement precalcination, minerals), yielding concentrated process CO2 for capture
trl_basis: Agora Industry/Fraunhofer ISI (2024): shock-wave (rotodynamic) heating 'Technology readiness level 6', pilot phase complete, commercial launch targeted before 2030. Integrated all-electric cement/lime kilns have no published TRL; VTT ran a pilot electric rotary kiln at ~1000C (2021-22) without stating a TRL
key_constraints: Very large grid connection; kiln replacement/rebuild; heat-transfer and clinker chemistry validation; electricity cost at high load factor
uk_status: None; international pilots (VTT Finland; Coolbrook demonstrations)
provenance: [AGORA2024] Shock-wave heating entry used as the rated route to electric kiln temperatures; VTT2022 documents the pilot - see challenges on scope

option_name: Electric powder-coating cure ovens
duty: Electric convection (or IR-assisted) cure ovens for powder coating lines (~160-200C), replacing gas-fired cure ovens
trl_basis: DESNZ/ERM rates industrial resistance heating TRL 9; electric powder-cure ovens are standard catalogue products
key_constraints: Higher running cost at current UK spark spread; supply capacity for larger batch/conveyor ovens; slower heat-up than direct gas in some designs
uk_status: Commercial; common at small/medium size, gas still dominant for large conveyorised ovens
provenance: [REF_RELIANT_OVENS] Equipment supplier comparison of gas vs electric powder cure ovens

option_name: Electric radiant/infrared space heating for high-bay workshops
duty: Electric infrared emitters providing spot/zone heating of occupied positions in high-bay, intermittently occupied or well-ventilated workshops
trl_basis: No published TRL located; catalogue commercial products
key_constraints: High electricity unit cost vs gas makes whole-building use expensive; best for spot/zone heating with low occupancy density; glare and mounting height limits
uk_status: Commercial; widely available; radiant heating equipment historically supported under the UK Energy Technology List
provenance: [REF_ECA_RADIANT] UK ETL datasheet ECA766 documents radiant heating suitability for high-bay industrial buildings (gas-fired focus); electric IR is the like-for-like electric variant

option_name: Electric resistance ovens and furnaces (incl. electric boosting)
duty: Ovens, dryers and furnaces from ~100C to >1000C; electric boosting of gas-fired glass furnaces
trl_basis: Agora Industry/Fraunhofer ISI (2024): resistance heating 'Technology readiness level 9 - established in specific applications'; Glass Futures for BEIS (2019): additional electric boosting 'is TRL8 at the moment'; large all-electric melting of big furnaces judged not yet feasible
key_constraints: Grid capacity; full furnace replacement (not burner retrofit) for direct-fired processes; scale limits for all-electric melting (>600 t/d glass); heat-transfer characteristics differ from flames
uk_status: Deployed for boosting and small furnaces/ovens; all-electric melting at container-glass scale under investigation (Glass Futures, IFS Phase 3)
provenance: [AGORA2024] TRL table for resistance heating; GLASSFUTURES2019 for the TRL8 boosting rating and scale caveat

option_name: Electrically heated steam cracker furnace
duty: Electric heating of olefin cracker furnaces in place of gas firing
trl_basis: 6 MW large-scale demonstration furnaces operating at BASF Ludwigshafen since April 2024 (system demonstration in operational environment per EU TRL definitions)
key_constraints: Very large firm low-carbon power demand; furnace replacement; olefin crackers only; full-scale commercial designs not yet offered
uk_status: No UK demonstration; relevant to remaining UK cracker capacity
provenance: [ecracker_2024] BASF/SABIC/Linde start-up press release

option_name: Electric drying hood / fully electric tissue machine
duty: Replace gas-fired yankee hoods and steam heating with electric hood and electric steam/heat pump on tissue machines
trl_basis: World-first fully electric tissue machine (Toscotec/Fortissue) reported operating at full speed, April 2025
key_constraints: Tissue machines only; large grid connection; electricity vs gas price; new-build or major rebuild
uk_status: No known UK installation; directly applicable to UK tissue mills
provenance: [toscotec_electric_2025] Trade press report of first fully electric tissue machine in operation

option_name: Fully electric tunnel kiln for clay tile/brick firing
duty: Continuous electric tunnel kiln firing clay roof tiles/bricks (~1000-1100C)
trl_basis: No numeric TRL located; described as world-first fully electric roof tile tunnel kiln, construction started at Wienerberger Broomfleet (UK) in 2026; precedent GreenBricks electric kiln in Austria
key_constraints: First-of-a-kind capex; grid connection and electricity price vs gas; firing-curve and atmosphere control for product colour; new-build rather than retrofit
uk_status: UK world-first under construction (Broomfleet, East Yorkshire)
provenance: [R_WIENERBERGER] Wienerberger UK announcement of world's first fully electric roof tile kiln

option_name: Electrified steam methane reforming (eSMR/eREACT)
duty: Resistance-heated catalytic steam reforming for syngas, hydrogen and methanol duties
trl_basis: Topsoe eSMR demonstration plant operating at Foulum, Denmark since 2021 (biogas-to-methanol); peer-reviewed pilot-plant study published
key_constraints: Needs firm low-carbon power; reformer replacement; early commercial offerings only
uk_status: No UK installation identified
provenance: [topsoe_esmr_2021] Topsoe press release on eSMR demonstration plant operation

option_name: Grid-connected static electric crushing/screening/washing plant (replacing diesel mobile plant)
duty: Fixed primary/secondary crushing, screening, washing at long-life consented sites
trl_basis: Standard commercial practice; OEMs market full electric static/'electric train' plant ranges (Hub-4, 2026)
key_constraints: Grid connection capacity and cost at rural sites; capital cost; less flexible than mobile plant as extraction faces move
uk_status: Widely deployed at UK quarries; grid capacity is the main barrier to further rollout
provenance: [REF_HUB4_2026] UK trade press on electric crushing/screening plant, sold from Sandvik Burton-on-Trent

option_name: Electrochemical synthesis routes
duty: Electrochemical/electrolytic synthesis replacing thermochemical process steps in chemicals manufacture
trl_basis: Mostly lab/bench scale per JACS Au review (2022); established exceptions (chlor-alkali, adiponitrile) already commercial
key_constraints: Electrode/membrane durability, selectivity, scale-up; product-specific; needs cheap low-carbon power
uk_status: Research and start-up activity; no bulk-scale UK deployment
provenance: [jacsau_echem_2022] Review of emerging electrochemical processes to decarbonise the chemical industry

option_name: Electric / electrode boilers (steam and hot water)
duty: Hot water and steam up to ~350C / >70 bar; unit sizes from <1 MW (resistance) to tens of MW (electrode)
trl_basis: TNO/energy.nl technology factsheet (Marsidi 2018): 'Current TRL level is 9, established technology'; Agora Industry/Fraunhofer ISI (2024): electric boilers 'Technology readiness level 9'; CCC/Element Energy assumptions log shows TRL9 achieved 2018 (small electric steam boiler), 2018-2030 (large electrode)
key_constraints: Grid connection capacity and cost of reinforcement; electricity-to-gas price ratio ('spark gap') dominates economics; minimal space/retrofit burden as steam interface unchanged
uk_status: Commercially available; limited UK deployment to date, mostly as hybrid/flex units; supported under IETF
provenance: [TNO_EBOILER2018] Factsheet header TRL field; corroborated by AGORA2024 technology table and CCC_LOG2019 rollout table p11

option_name: Electrolytic (green) hydrogen integration at refineries
duty: On-site electrolytic hydrogen displacing SMR hydrogen for hydrotreating/hydrocracking
trl_basis: 10 MW PEM electrolyser operating within Shell Rheinland refinery since 2021 (REFHYNE); 100 MW follow-on planned
key_constraints: Electrolyser capex and power price; small versus total refinery H2 demand; grid capacity
uk_status: Proposed at UK refineries (e.g. Gigastack/Humber); none operating
provenance: [refhyne_2021] REFHYNE start-up of Europe's largest PEM electrolyser at a refinery

option_name: EV fleet depot charging infrastructure
duty: Depot/workplace charge points, grid connection upgrades and smart charging enabling electrification of vans, company vehicles and customer fleets
trl_basis: Mature commercial technology; no formal TRL located
key_constraints: Grid connection capacity and upgrade lead times; dwell-time vs charge-rate matching; enabler only — emissions saving accrues to the vehicle fleet
uk_status: Fully commercial; supported by Energy Saving Trust fleet guidance and past Workplace Charging Scheme grants
provenance: [REF_EST_FLEET] Energy Saving Trust guidance on charging business electric vehicles at depots/workplaces

option_name: Fab low-grade heat recovery to HVAC/process
duty: Recover low-grade fab heat (process cooling water, heat-recovery chillers) to heat cleanroom makeup air and offset gas boilers
trl_basis: Deployed at scale by Intel (heat-recovery chillers / hot water reuse reported 2023)
key_constraints: Low source temperatures (30-40C); hydraulic integration and space in retrofit; largest benefit in new builds
uk_status: Applicable to UK fabs; no published UK example located
provenance: [intel_heat_recovery] Report on Intel using recovered hot water to cut fab natural gas use

option_name: Fast firing / low thermal mass kiln technology
duty: Roller-hearth/fast-fire kilns and low-mass kiln furniture reducing specific firing energy
trl_basis: Commercially deployed for tiles and tableware; identified in BEIS/BCC 2015 ceramics decarbonisation roadmap technology options
key_constraints: Product-dependent (thick heavy-clay ware cannot fast-fire); requires kiln replacement capex at end-of-life; quality control
uk_status: Commercial in whitewares; limited applicability heavy clay
provenance: [R_BEIS_CER2015] BEIS/BCC ceramics sector roadmap 2015 covers kiln efficiency/fast firing options

option_name: Fermentation CO2 recovery, purification and liquefaction
duty: Capture of high-purity biogenic CO2 from fermentation vessels for reuse in carbonation/packaging or sale/sequestration
trl_basis: No formal TRL located; commercial packaged systems offered by multiple vendors and standard at large breweries per vendor and peer-reviewed craft-brewing literature
key_constraints: Economics weak at small scale (capture, purification and liquefaction cost); food-grade purity standards; intermittent fermentation profile needs buffering
uk_status: Commercial at large UK breweries; distillery deployments emerging (Whyte & Mackay with Carbon Capture Scotland; Ardgowan novel-capture pilot)
provenance: [HW_CO2_VAL] Heriot-Watt study of fermentation CO2 valorisation in craft brewing; Atlas Copco UK brewery CO2 recovery product line; W&M and Ardgowan distillery projects

option_name: Fume cupboard VAV and sash management
duty: VAV fume cupboard controls, sash-closure programmes and face-velocity optimisation cutting exhaust of conditioned air
trl_basis: Commercial controls documented in I2SL Smart Labs Toolkit and university guidance
key_constraints: Containment safety assessment required; benefit depends on cupboard density and existing controls
uk_status: Widely applied across UK universities and pharma R&D
provenance: [smartlabs_toolkit] I2SL Smart Labs Toolkit assessment guidance

option_name: Electrification of gas compression (electric motor VSD drives replacing gas turbines/engines)
duty: Electric motor-driven export/process compression at gas terminals and installations
trl_basis: Electric-drive compression is established technology; NSTA (2024) reports UK electrification projects underway (e.g. Buzzard) — no numeric TRL published
key_constraints: Large grid connection (tens of MW); brownfield conversion cost and downtime; remaining asset life must justify investment
uk_status: NSTA-driven electrification programme for offshore/onshore assets; draft OGA Plan requires operators to assess electrification
provenance: [REF_NSTA24] NSTA workshop and OGA Plan on electrification of UK oil and gas assets

option_name: Grid-powered (highline) and hybrid-battery electric drilling rigs
duty: Rig power from grid connection or battery-hybrid gensets instead of diesel-only gensets
trl_basis: Ipieca energy efficiency compendium (2023): commercially available with 5-10 years industry experience; up to 100% GHG reduction with low-carbon grid power
key_constraints: Temporary grid connection cost/lead time for short campaigns; rural network capacity; hybrid option only partial abatement
uk_status: Applicable to limited UK onshore drilling; hybrid gensets deployable now
provenance: [REF_IPIECA23] Industry compendium entry specifically on drilling rig electrification/hybridisation

option_name: Hydrogen-fired boilers (steam/hot water)
duty: Steam and hot water across standard boiler ranges (incl. package boilers, waste-heat recovery boilers)
trl_basis: HyNet Industrial Fuel Switching (Progressive Energy, 2022): waste heat recovery boilers 'already available to fire on 100% Hydrogen... TRL of 9'; package boiler switching demonstrated over 4 weeks in Phase 2; Hy4Heat WP6 (Element Energy, 2019): 'around 25 demonstrations are required to reach TRL 9 across the key costed equipment types'; CCC/Element Energy assumptions log: 100% H2 boilers reach TRL9 ~2025
key_constraints: Low-carbon hydrogen supply and pipeline connection (cluster dependence); NOx control (FGR/staged burners); on-site storage and DSEAR zoning; burner/valve-train retrofit
uk_status: Demonstrated (HyNet trials at Unilever Port Sunlight boiler, 2021-22); commercial rollout awaits H2 networks
provenance: [HYNET2022] TRL9 quote for WHRBs and Phase 2 boiler trial; HY4HEAT2019 and CCC_LOG2019 for the wider band

option_name: Hydrogen direct reduced iron (H2-DRI) feeding EAF
duty: Ore-based primary ironmaking: shaft-furnace reduction of iron ore with green hydrogen, product (DRI/HBI) melted in EAF, replacing BF-BOF route
trl_basis: Green Steel for Europe technology assessment (2021) rates hydrogen direct reduction ~TRL 7; HYBRIT pilot produced hydrogen-reduced sponge iron in 2021 and a demonstration plant is in development at Gallivare
key_constraints: Requires large volumes of low-carbon hydrogen and electricity; DR-grade ore pellets; new-build plant; EAF melting capacity downstream
uk_status: No UK DRI plant; Port Talbot and Scunthorpe transitions are scrap-EAF based, but imported H2-DRI/HBI could feed future UK EAFs
provenance: [REF_HYBRIT] SSAB/LKAB/Vattenfall HYBRIT pilot results; TRL from Green Steel for Europe assessment (REF_GS4E)

option_name: Hydrogen firing of kilns, furnaces, ovens and dryers (direct-fired)
duty: Direct-fired process heat from ~200C dryers to >1500C melting furnaces and kilns
trl_basis: HyNet/Essity IFS feasibility (2022): hydrogen burners and paper drying 'are all deployed commercially, but a combination of the two is currently around TRL 5. By the end of the demonstration... TRL 8'; Glass Futures for BEIS (2019): 'full-scale pure hydrogen firing is at a low TRL'; HyNet Phase 2 demonstrated H2 melting of float glass with 'good heat transfer'; CCC/Element Energy log: H2-fired kiln TRL9 ~2026
key_constraints: H2 supply/cluster location; changed flame radiation and moisture affects product quality (glass, ceramics, lime); NOx; application-specific trials required per Hy4Heat
uk_status: Demonstration (NSG Pilkington 100% H2 float glass trial 2021; DESNZ IFS Phase 3 demos in glass, lime, cement fuel mix)
provenance: [ESSITY2022] Explicit TRL5-to-8 statement; GLASSFUTURES2019, HYNET2022, CCC_LOG2019, DESNZ_IFS3_2022 corroborate range

option_name: Hydrogen-ready boilers and combustion equipment (buy-now, convert-later)
duty: New natural-gas equipment designed for 'easier, cheaper, and faster conversion' to 100% hydrogen; any boiler/burner duty
trl_basis: No published TRL located. BEIS call for evidence (2021) states 'there is currently no standardised definition of hydrogen-ready for industrial boiler equipment' and that few sites are taking preparatory steps
key_constraints: Definition/standards immature; residual conversion cost and outage; only valuable where future H2 network credible; risk of stranded 'readiness' premium
uk_status: Policy development stage; some OEMs market dual-fuel/H2-capable burners
provenance: [BEIS_H2READY2021] CfE pp. on definition and market status; TRL null per rules

option_name: DRI/HBI charging to EAF (natural-gas DRI, H2-ready)
duty: Blending merchant DRI/HBI with scrap in EAF to dilute residuals and enable flat/high-grade products; NG-based today, convertible to hydrogen
trl_basis: MIDREX/HYL natural-gas DRI plants and HBI charging to EAFs are commercially operated worldwide (Midrex technical literature)
key_constraints: DRI/HBI supply chain and price; NG-DRI still emits CO2 unless converted to H2 or fitted with CCS; melting energy higher than scrap
uk_status: No UK DRI production; HBI import to future UK EAFs is a recognised quality lever
provenance: [REF_MIDREX] Midrex tech article on ore-based metallics and hydrogen pathways for EAF steelmaking

option_name: Heat pump concepts >200C
duty: Steam/process heat above 200C (lab-scale concepts)
trl_basis: de Boer et al. (2020): 'Development of 3 technologies at a laboratory scale (1 kW to 10 kW), demonstrating the technical feasibility of heat pump concepts to supply heat at temperatures above 200C. (TRL3-5)'
key_constraints: Working fluids and compressor materials at extreme lift; no commercial products; long development timeline
uk_status: None (laboratory only)
provenance: [DEBOER2020] >200C entry of TRL list

option_name: Industrial heat pumps <100C (commercial-class)
duty: Hot water/low-pressure heat below 100C: washing, pasteurisation, space heat, drying make-up air
trl_basis: de Boer et al. (2020) white paper: 'Heat pump technology is established as the reference (low carbon) technology for heat supply <100C, with at least 500 large scale (1 MW to 10 MW) units installed... (TRL9)'
key_constraints: Needs an accessible low-grade heat source (waste heat, ambient, effluent); grid connection; space for heat exchangers; COP falls with temperature lift
uk_status: Deployed; multiple UK installs incl. IETF-supported food & drink projects
provenance: [DEBOER2020] Innovation target/status list, <100C entry

option_name: Heat-recovery heat pumps (upgrading waste heat to process temperature)
duty: Upgrading 20-70C waste heat to 60-150C useful heat/LP steam
trl_basis: de Boer et al. (2020): TRL9 below 100C supply; IEA HPT Annex 58 (2023) documents 18 demonstration cases (food/beverage, refinery, chemicals) and commercial availability up to ~120C in 2024-25 - upper band (to 150C) TRL 8
key_constraints: Reliable waste-heat stream; temperature lift limits COP; grid capacity; integration engineering
uk_status: Deployed/demonstration (IETF-supported installs in food & drink)
provenance: [ANNEX58_2023] Demonstration case studies + availability timeline; DEBOER2020 for <100C TRL9

option_name: HIsarna smelting reduction (coke-free ironmaking)
duty: Direct smelting of ore fines with coal, eliminating coke ovens and sinter plant; ~20% CO2 saving, up to ~80% with CCS on the concentrated CO2 off-gas
trl_basis: 60 kt/y pilot plant operated at Tata Steel IJmuiden through multiple campaigns; no industrial-scale demonstration built (Global Energy Monitor / Tata publications)
key_constraints: Requires new-build vessel; scale-up risk; CCS needed for deep abatement; Tata's focus has shifted to DRI-EAF
uk_status: No UK deployment; originally developed partly by Tata Steel (ex-Corus UK R&D involvement)
provenance: [REF_HISARNA] Global Energy Monitor summary of HIsarna process status and pilot campaigns

option_name: High-temperature heat pumps 100-150C
duty: Low-pressure steam and hot processes 100-150C: evaporation, drying, sterilisation, distillation reboil
trl_basis: IEA HPT Annex 58 Task 1 (2023): reviewed HTHP solutions span TRL 4-9, commercially available 'up to 120C' 2024-25 and 'up to 160C' 2025-26; de Boer et al. (2020) frame TRL8 at 100-150C (25 full-scale demos); Agora (2024): industrial heat pumps 'TRL 8 (at very high temperatures and high capacities) - 9'
key_constraints: Grid connection; heat-source temperature/quantity; limited supplier and service network; higher capex than boilers; integration/retrofit engineering
uk_status: Early commercial/demonstration in UK; supplier products available (steam-generating heat pumps)
provenance: [ANNEX58_2023] Executive summary commercial-availability timeline; DEBOER2020 TRL band; AGORA2024 table. de Boer figures are partly framed as demo-count targets - see challenges

option_name: Very-high-temperature heat pumps 150-200C
duty: Medium-pressure steam and process heat 150-200C
trl_basis: de Boer et al. (2020): 'Up to 5 pilot scale (+/-100 kW) demonstration projects to validate the technical feasibility of industrial heat pumps to supply heat beyond 150C. (TRL6-7)'; Annex 58 (2023) notes 'considerable effort needed to develop and demonstrate' at these temperatures
key_constraints: As 100-150C plus refrigerant/compressor limits at high lift; efficiency and cost unproven at scale; few reference plants
uk_status: Pilot/prototype internationally; no known UK commercial install
provenance: [DEBOER2020] >150C entry of TRL list; ANNEX58_2023 for status corroboration

option_name: HVO and bio-oils as drop-in fuel (mobile plant, standby generation, heating oil replacement)
duty: Direct diesel/gas-oil substitute in existing engines, mobile plant and standby boilers/generators; no equipment change
trl_basis: IEA Bioenergy Task 39 (2024): the HVO/HEFA pathway 'has already achieved commercial status' (commercial = top of the report's TRL framework); ETIP Bioenergy factsheet (2020): 'The production of HVO is well-developed at industrial scale'; DESNZ NRMM CfE summary (2025): 'HVO was reported to be an effective drop-in replacement for diesel, without impacting on performance'
key_constraints: Feedstock sustainability/verification (UCO fraud risk raised in CfE responses); price premium over diesel; supply competition with aviation (HEFA)
uk_status: Deployed - widely used on UK construction sites and for standby generation
provenance: [IEABIO_T39_2024] Commercial-status statement mapped to TRL 9 of the report's own framework (Table 2) - mapping noted in challenges; ETIP_HVO2020 and DESNZ_NRMM_CFE2025 corroborate

option_name: Hydrogen fuel-cell/battery hybrid ultra-class haul truck (nuGen-type)
duty: Zero-emission haulage for large rigid haul trucks (100t+ payload)
trl_basis: Single 2MW prototype (Anglo American nuGen) demonstrated in operational mine environment since 2022; not a commercial product
key_constraints: On-site hydrogen production/refuelling; very high cost; no OEM series product; UK quarry truck sizes smaller than demo class
uk_status: No UK activity; overseas demonstration only
provenance: [REF_ANGLO22] OEM press release for world-first hydrogen haul truck prototype

option_name: Hydrogen mobile plant (fuel cell and H2 combustion engine NRMM)
duty: Motive power for heavy, high-utilisation machinery where batteries impractical; H2 gensets
trl_basis: No numeric TRL extracted. ERM study for DESNZ (2023): hydrogen fuel cell 'in development'; DESNZ CfE summary (2025): respondents report 'hydrogen fuel cell machinery, such as generators, are already commercially available' and suggest 'hydrogen ICE should be assumed to be available sooner... by 2030'
key_constraints: On-site H2 supply, storage and refuelling; fuel cost; regulations (storage, RTFO treatment); early OEM offerings only (e.g. JCB H2 ICE)
uk_status: Demonstration/pilot (JCB hydrogen ICE machines; fuel-cell gensets on construction sites)
provenance: [DESNZ_NRMM_CFE2025] Respondent statements; ERM_NRMM2023 for development status; TRL null per rules

option_name: Impingement / through-air drying conversion
duty: High-intensity impingement or through-air drying sections raising drying rates and enabling fuel-switched (H2/electric) hoods
trl_basis: TAD and impingement hoods commercially established in tissue; UK roadmap lists advanced drying technologies among options
key_constraints: Air-based drying is gas-fired unless paired with electric or H2 heating; TAD raises specific energy (used for quality); machine rebuild
uk_status: TAD installed at some UK tissue sites
provenance: [paper_roadmap_2015] UK pulp & paper 2050 roadmap covers advanced drying options

option_name: High reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) content
duty: Recycle planings into new asphalt, cutting embodied carbon of binder and aggregate
trl_basis: Commercially deployed; UK producers market mixes with high RAP contents at standard plants
key_constraints: Specification limits on RAP %; RAP supply/quality consistency; high-RAP operation needs plant modifications (parallel drum/superheating); modest effect on plant fuel per tonne
uk_status: Commercial and growing across UK plants
provenance: [R_RAP] Holcim UK recycled asphalt page describing RAP use in UK production

option_name: Induction heating and melting
duty: Heating/melting of electrically conductive materials (metals) to >1200C; forging, hardening, melting
trl_basis: Agora Industry/Fraunhofer ISI (2024): induction heating 'Technology readiness level 9 - Established technology in metal processing'
key_constraints: Limited to conductive workpieces; high power draw and grid connection; furnace replacement rather than burner retrofit
uk_status: Deployed (metals processing, foundries)
provenance: [AGORA2024] TRL table, induction entry; HASANBEIGI2021 corroborates commercial status

option_name: Inert anode aluminium electrolysis (ELYSIS)
displaces: carbon anodes (process CO2); anode baking fuel
duty: Replacing consumable carbon anodes with inert anodes in Hall-Heroult cells, eliminating direct process CO2 and PFC emissions (oxygen by-product)
trl_basis: ELYSIS (Alcoa/Rio Tinto) started up a commercial-size 450 kA cell with inert anodes in 2025 — first-of-a-kind demonstration at commercial scale
key_constraints: Anode life and cost; cell energy balance changes (loss of carbon oxidation heat); retrofit to existing potlines unproven; licensing just beginning
uk_status: Not deployed at Lochaber (UK's only smelter, hydro-powered); a long-term option for its process CO2
provenance: [REF_ELYSIS] Rio Tinto press release on ELYSIS commercial-size inert anode cell start-up

option_name: Thermal insulation of plant, pipework and furnaces (incl. refractory upgrade)
duty: Reduces standing losses on steam systems, tanks, furnaces; all temperature ranges
trl_basis: No published TRL located; mature commercial products outside TRL frameworks in the sources reviewed
key_constraints: Access/outage for hot works; none technical
uk_status: Deployed; persistent economic potential
provenance: [HASANBEIGI2021] TRL null per rules; context reference only

option_name: Inverter welding power sources
duty: Replacement of transformer-rectifier welding sets with inverter power sources, cutting conversion losses and idle draw in welding and body shops
trl_basis: Mature commercial technology per manufacturer literature; no formal TRL located
key_constraints: Modest absolute savings unless welding-intensive; equipment refresh cycle driven; power quality/harmonics on large installations
uk_status: Fully commercial; default for new purchases
provenance: [REF_LINCOLN_INVERTER] Lincoln Electric technical article on inverter power source energy efficiency

option_name: In-pit crushing and conveying (IPCC) / conveyor haulage replacing dump trucks
duty: Replace diesel truck haulage from face to plant with in-pit crusher plus electric conveyors
trl_basis: Technology in commercial use for decades; documented emissions-reduction driver (Worley; Snowden Optiro)
key_constraints: High capex; reduces mine-plan flexibility; suits long-life, high-tonnage operations with stable haul routes
uk_status: Field conveyors common at larger UK quarries; full IPCC rare at UK scale
provenance: [REF_WORLEY] Industry analysis of IPCC as sustainability/decarbonisation measure vs truck-shovel

option_name: Low-temperature iron ore electrowinning (SIDERWIN/Volteron)
duty: Alkaline electrolysis of iron ore at ~110C producing iron plate for EAF melting, zero direct CO2 with clean power
trl_basis: EU H2020 SIDERWIN project demonstrated the electrochemical cell at pilot scale (CORDIS results article); ArcelorMittal-John Cockerill 'Volteron' industrial-scale plant announced
key_constraints: Low current density means large cell areas; scale-up unproven; high electricity demand; product must be melted in EAF
uk_status: No UK activity
provenance: [REF_SIDERWIN] CORDIS results article on SIDERWIN electrolysis pilot; ArcelorMittal/John Cockerill industrial plant announcement (REF_VOLTERON)

option_name: Kiln-to-dryer cascade heat recovery (tunnel kiln cooling zone heat)
duty: Recover hot air from kiln cooling zones to feed dryers in brick/tile/ceramics works
trl_basis: Established industry practice discussed in BEIS/BCC 2015 ceramics roadmap
key_constraints: Couples kiln and dryer scheduling; retrofit ducting; many UK sites already do this, limiting incremental savings; conflicts with kiln electrification (less waste heat)
uk_status: Widely deployed; further optimisation potential
provenance: [R_BEIS_CER2015] BEIS/BCC ceramics roadmap covers heat recovery from kilns to dryers

option_name: Net-zero kiln fuel mix (hydrogen + biomass wastes) for cement/lime kilns
duty: Main-burner fuel mix of hydrogen, meat and bone meal and glycerine demonstrated at commercial cement kiln scale
trl_basis: No numeric TRL located; world-first commercial-scale trial completed at Hanson/Heidelberg Ribblesdale (2021) under BEIS fuel-switching programme
key_constraints: Hydrogen supply/cost and onsite storage; burner and flame-profile modifications; biomass by-product availability; addresses combustion CO2 only (~40% of cement emissions)
uk_status: Demonstrated at Ribblesdale cement works; academic study confirmed success
provenance: [R_MPA_RIBB] MPA press release on world-first net zero fuel mix trial at Ribblesdale

option_name: Lab air-change-rate reduction with demand-controlled ventilation
duty: Risk-based ACH reduction with air-quality sensing and demand-controlled ventilation
trl_basis: Commercial systems with documented case studies (WBDG / Smart Labs)
key_constraints: Hazard assessment and governance of setpoints; sensor maintenance
uk_status: Growing UK uptake in university and commercial labs
provenance: [wbdg_ach_2022] WBDG resource on reducing lab air change rates

option_name: Lab exhaust heat recovery (run-around coils)
duty: Run-around coil/plate heat recovery on 100% outside-air laboratory ventilation
trl_basis: Established best practice per Labs21/NREL guide
key_constraints: Contamination risk rules out wheels in many labs (run-around preferred); added fan power; retrofit space
uk_status: Standard in new UK lab buildings; large retrofit potential in older stock
provenance: [nrel_labs21_erv] Labs for the 21st Century best practice guide on energy recovery

option_name: LED lighting with occupancy/daylight controls (labs)
duty: LED retrofit and occupancy sensing in lab and write-up spaces
trl_basis: Commercial; lab occupancy-sensor implementation case study (I2SL Smart Labs)
key_constraints: Sensor placement in cellular lab spaces; small share of total lab energy versus HVAC
uk_status: Standard retrofit measure in UK estates
provenance: [emory_lighting_case] Smart Labs case study on occupancy sensors in labs

option_name: LED high-bay lighting with controls
duty: Replacement of HID/fluorescent high-bay luminaires with LED plus occupancy/daylight controls in workshops, factories and sortation halls
trl_basis: Mature commercial technology; no formal TRL rating located
key_constraints: Capex only; interaction with heating (reduced internal gains) marginal; emergency lighting compliance on retrofit
uk_status: Fully commercial and default retrofit; typically 50%+ lighting energy saving per Carbon Trust guidance
provenance: [REF_CT_LIGHTING] Carbon Trust Lighting overview guide covers LED retrofit and controls

option_name: LED-UV curing replacing gas-fired dryers
duty: Instant-cure LED-UV inks replacing gas heatset/IR dryers on web and sheetfed presses
trl_basis: Commercially available; European web printers reported converting from gas heatset dryers to LED-UV (trade press)
key_constraints: Ink cost premium; substrate/ink compatibility; coldset newsprint has no dryer so limited relevance there
uk_status: Commercially available and adopted by some UK commercial printers
provenance: [baldwin_leduv] Baldwin/trade report on heatset-to-LED-UV conversions

option_name: Oxyfuel flash calcination of lime with inherent CO2 capture (Origen ZerCaL)
duty: Flash calciner producing quicklime with concentrated capture-ready CO2 stream
trl_basis: No numeric TRL located; demonstration kiln commissioning reported by developer; ZerCaL250 project proposed in Humber
key_constraints: First-of-a-kind; oxygen supply; lime product quality/reactivity; needs CO2 transport and storage offtake
uk_status: UK developer (Origen); demonstration stage, proposed UK deployment
provenance: [R_ORIGEN] Origen news on kiln commissioning; Invest Humber ZerCaL250 listing corroborates UK project

option_name: Low-bake / low-temperature-cure paint chemistry
duty: Reformulated OEM coatings curing at reduced oven temperatures (~80-120C vs 140-180C), cutting paint-shop oven fuel use and enabling oven electrification
trl_basis: US DOE advanced coatings workshop (2016) discusses low-temperature-cure automotive coatings as a development priority; no formal TRL published
key_constraints: Requires OEM paint requalification (appearance, durability, corrosion warranty); coating supplier lock-in; benefits depend on oven redesign
uk_status: OEM/supplier trials (e.g. BASF, PPG low-cure systems); not standard practice in UK plants
provenance: [REF_DOE_COATINGS] US DOE workshop report on advanced coatings for automotive applications covers low-temperature cure

option_name: Low-GWP process gas substitution
duty: Substituting high-GWP etch/clean gases (CF4, SF6) with low-GWP alternatives (e.g. C3F6, C2F4O)
trl_basis: Laboratory plasma etch studies published (ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering, 2025)
key_constraints: Per-tool, per-recipe requalification; etch performance parity unproven at production scale
uk_status: Research stage; no UK production use identified
provenance: [acs_lowgwp_2025] Peer-reviewed study of low-GWP CF4 replacement etch gas

option_name: Low-temperature / alternative tanning chemistry
duty: Alternative tanning/retanning chemistries and float management reducing hot-water and drying energy
trl_basis: No published TRL located; chrome-free/low-float systems commercially offered; UNIDO framework discusses cleaner process options
key_constraints: Leather quality and customer acceptance; process requalification; energy-saving evidence site-specific
uk_status: Some UK tanneries trialling chrome-free systems; uptake limited
provenance: [unido_framework_2019] UNIDO framework for sustainable leather manufacture

option_name: Heat-pump kilning with kiln exhaust heat recovery
duty: Large heat pumps recovering latent heat from humid kiln exhaust to supply ~60-90C kiln air, replacing gas-fired air heating
trl_basis: No published TRL; full-scale projects in planning/execution (Boortmalt Bury St Edmunds planning application 2024, described as its second large-scale heat pump project)
key_constraints: Kiln airflow/temperature profile (curing phase hottest); large electrical connection; fouling of exhaust heat exchangers; malt quality/flavour validation
uk_status: Demonstration stage in UK malting; Boortmalt Bury St Edmunds (100kt/yr) plans ~9,150 tCO2/yr saving
provenance: [BOORTMALT_HP] Boortmalt planning application for heat-pump decarbonisation of Bury St Edmunds maltings

option_name: Microwave-assisted firing/sintering of ceramics
duty: Hybrid microwave plus conventional heating to cut firing energy and cycle time
trl_basis: No numeric TRL located; long-standing R&D (UK IET conference paper 1998; recent lab studies) with no industrial-scale deployment identified
key_constraints: Heating uniformity and susceptor issues; scale-up beyond kW-scale kilns; product-specific validation; retrofit difficulty
uk_status: UK R&D heritage, no industrial deployment found
provenance: [R_MW_IET] IET 'Microwave-assisted firing of ceramics'; recent MDPI study (R_MW_MDPI) confirms continued lab-scale status

option_name: Microwave / radio-frequency dielectric heating and drying
duty: Volumetric drying/heating of dielectric materials: food, chemicals drying, freeze-drying assist; novel uses (pyrolysis, minerals) lower TRL
trl_basis: CalNEXT/AESC Industrial Microwave Technologies Market Study (2024): food processing 'estimated TRL is 7 to 9'; chemicals 'For simple drying applications, the current estimated TRL is 7 to 9'; complex reactions (e.g. pyrolysis) TRL 3-6; metallurgy TRL 3-4
key_constraints: Product dielectric properties determine suitability; per-line engineering; magnetron/solid-state source costs; scale-up beyond drying unproven
uk_status: Commercial in food niches (tempering, drying); demonstration elsewhere
provenance: [CALNEXT2024] Sector-by-sector TRL estimates; TRL given applies to drying duties only

option_name: Minewater heat recovery via heat pumps (heat networks / building heat)
duty: Extract low-grade heat (~15-20C) from pumped minewater at treatment/pumping schemes and upgrade with heat pumps for heat offtakers
trl_basis: Gateshead 6MW minewater heat network fully operational since March 2023 (GOV.UK); Coal Authority Dawdon/Seaham scheme in development
key_constraints: Needs nearby heat demand; displaces offtakers' gas rather than site's own fuel; ochre fouling of heat exchangers; long-term coordination with Mining Remediation Authority
uk_status: Operational (Gateshead); further Coal Authority schemes in development (Seaham/Dawdon)
provenance: [REF_GOVUK_GATESHEAD] Official confirmation of operational UK minewater heat scheme

option_name: Molten oxide electrolysis of iron ore (Boston Metal)
duty: Direct electrolytic reduction of iron ore to liquid metal at ~1600C using inert anodes, zero direct CO2 with clean power
trl_basis: Independent technology assessment (Thunder Said Energy) places MOE at pilot stage (~TRL 4-5); Boston Metal operating semi-industrial cells, commercial demo planned late 2020s
key_constraints: Inert anode durability at 1600C; very high electricity demand; scale-up from pilot cells; no continuous industrial operation yet
uk_status: No UK activity
provenance: [REF_BOSTON] Thunder Said Energy technology review of Boston Metal MOE; company fact sheet (REF_BOSTON_FS)

option_name: Mechanical vapour recompression (MVR)
duty: Recompression of process vapour/waste steam to useful pressure (~2.5-4.5 bar up to ~13 bar); evaporation, distillation, concentration duties
trl_basis: TNO/energy.nl factsheet 'Industrial mechanical vapour recompression' (Marsidi 2018): 'TRL 9'; ARENA/Alcoa (2022): 'MVR is an established technology' though first-of-a-kind at alumina-refinery scale
key_constraints: Needs a clean, condensable vapour stream at suitable pressure; compressor sizing/fouling; grid connection; novel at very large single-train scale
uk_status: Commercial in evaporation-heavy sectors (food, chemicals, effluent); site-specific
provenance: [TNO_MVR2018] Factsheet TRL field; ARENA_MVR2022 for scale caveat

option_name: High-efficiency natural refrigerant (NH3/CO2) refrigeration replacement
duty: Replace ageing HFC/R22 plant with efficient ammonia or transcritical CO2 systems, often with integrated heat recovery
trl_basis: No formal TRL; mature commercial technology with large UK installations (e.g. multi-MW ammonia plant at NewCold cold store)
key_constraints: Ammonia safety case (DSEAR); CO2 efficiency at high ambient; capex vs drop-in refrigerant swap; F-gas phase-down timing
uk_status: Fully commercial in UK food cold chain; F-gas regulation is driving conversion
provenance: [STAR_NATREF] Star Refrigeration guidance on natural refrigerant options under tightening F-gas rules; NewCold ammonia installation

option_name: Ohmic (direct resistance) heating of pumpable foods
duty: Direct volumetric electric heating for pasteurisation/sterilisation/cooking of pumpable and particulate foods
trl_basis: No formal TRL; peer-reviewed reviews report commercial ohmic installations for fruit, ready meals and liquid foods
key_constraints: Product must be pumpable with suitable conductivity; electrode fouling/corrosion; niche equipment supply; validation burden
uk_status: Commercially available at niche scale; limited UK penetration
provenance: [OHMIC_REVIEW] Peer-reviewed review of ohmic heating technology, applications and commercial status

option_name: Onsite solar PV (roof/ground) for site electricity
duty: Decarbonises/reduces grid electricity purchase; pairs with electrified heat and NRMM charging; no process heat directly
trl_basis: No numeric TRL located in sources reviewed; IEA describes solar PV among 'well established solar technologies'. (The IEA ETP Clean Energy Technology Guide rates PV but its interactive TRLs could not be programmatically verified - see challenges)
key_constraints: Roof condition/area; export/grid connection agreements; only abates electricity (relevant where sites electrify); planning for ground-mount
uk_status: Deployed widely on UK industrial roofs
provenance: [IEA_SOLARPV] Qualitative maturity statement only; TRL null per rules

option_name: Oxyfuel combustion capture
duty: Combustion in O2/recycled flue gas giving capture-ready CO2-rich flue; kilns and boilers
trl_basis: IEA CCUS in Clean Energy Transitions (2020): oxy-fuelling 'currently at the large prototype or pre-demonstration stage (TRL 5 to 7)'; Islam & Patlolla (2025) also rate oxyfuel 'TRL 5 to 7'
key_constraints: Air separation unit cost/energy; kiln/burner redesign and air-ingress sealing (retrofit-heavy); CO2 T&S dependence
uk_status: None; cement demos in EU (e.g. Heidelberg/CEMCAP lineage, catch4climate)
provenance: [IEA_CCUS2020] Capture-technology TRL section; ISLAM2025 concurs

option_name: Paint shop oven and booth heat recovery / air recirculation
duty: Heat recovery on paint cure-oven exhaust, spray-booth air recirculation and heat-wheel/runaround recovery on booth make-up air in vehicle paint shops
trl_basis: Documented as commercial measures in the ENERGY STAR vehicle assembly guide; no formal TRL published
key_constraints: Fouling of heat exchangers by paint overspray/VOC condensates; recirculation limited by solvent concentration and humidity control; retrofit space
uk_status: Commercial; standard in modern OEM paint shops, retrofittable to older UK plants
provenance: [REF_ESTAR_VEHICLE] ENERGY STAR vehicle assembly guide details paint-shop oven and booth energy measures

option_name: Point-of-use F-gas abatement and gas optimisation
duty: POU plasma/burn-wet abatement and process gas optimisation for PFC/NF3/SF6 from etch and chamber clean
trl_basis: World Semiconductor Council best-practice guidance; POU abatement commercially deployed industry-wide
key_constraints: Addresses non-CO2 F-gases rather than energy CO2; fuel-fired combustion abatement adds gas use (electric plasma variants avoid this); capex per tool
uk_status: Standard practice at UK fabs for new tools
provenance: [wsc_pfc_2012] WSC best practice guidance for PFC emission reduction

option_name: Electric plasma cutting replacing oxy-fuel torch cutting
duty: Electric plasma arc (and laser for plate) cutting of steel in place of oxy-fuel gas torches for scrap sizing, ship dismantling and plate prep
trl_basis: Plasma cutting is mature commercial technology; industry technical comparisons (ESAB) define capability envelope vs oxy-fuel
key_constraints: Practical thickness limit (~50-160 mm depending on system) — thick sections still need oxy-fuel; needs electrical supply at point of use, limiting hand-held field cutting on large scrap
uk_status: Commercially available and widely used in UK fabrication; partial substitution potential at scrap yards and shipyards
provenance: [REF_ESAB] ESAB technical comparison of oxy-fuel vs plasma cutting capabilities

option_name: Plasma torch process heating
duty: Very high temperature heat (>1500C flame equivalents) for kilns, calcination, melting
trl_basis: Agora Industry/Fraunhofer ISI (2024): plasma torches 'Technology readiness level 7-9' (small capacities established, clinker-burning applications need development); Svensson et al. (2021, Frontiers in Climate) describe plasma calcination of lime as 'a low TRL level' application while plasma is 'used in the metallurgical industry for melting, remelting and refining'
key_constraints: Electrode life and torch power limits; very high power density grid demand; integration into rotary kilns unproven at scale
uk_status: None known for process heat; torch hardware commercially available
provenance: [AGORA2024] TRL range is for torches; specific kiln/calcination integrations are lower (SVENSSON2021) - the two sources are combined in this range

option_name: Plug-in/grid-connected electric mobile crushers and screens
duty: Mobile crushing and screening run from grid connection or renewable supply instead of onboard diesel
trl_basis: Commercially available product ranges (e.g. Sandvik UJ443E jaw, QH443E cone, QA452e screen) with external grid connection option (Hub-4, 2026)
key_constraints: Site power supply and trailing cable management; genset fallback often still diesel/HVO; higher capex
uk_status: Commercially available in UK; growing uptake at quarries and recycling sites
provenance: [REF_HUB4_2026] Article specifically on electric mobile crushing/screening for quarrying

option_name: Post-combustion CO2 capture (amine/chemical absorption)
duty: Capture of flue-gas CO2 from boilers, kilns, furnaces, CHP; retrofit to existing combustion
trl_basis: IEA CCUS in Clean Energy Transitions (2020): chemical absorption is the 'most advanced CO2 separation technique (TRL 9-11)' on the IEA 1-11 scale; Islam & Patlolla (2025, Energies): 'At TRL 9-11, amine-based chemical absorption represents the most advanced CO2 separation technique'
key_constraints: CO2 transport & storage network dependence (cluster sequencing); large steam demand for solvent regeneration; footprint for absorber/stripper; capture economics need policy support
uk_status: First-of-a-kind under construction: Heidelberg Materials Padeswood cement CCS (HyNet) took FID 25 Sep 2025, construction started Dec 2025 (MHI amine capture)
provenance: [IEA_CCUS2020] Capture-technology TRL section; ISLAM2025 concurs; HEIDELBERG2025 for UK status

option_name: Process-free CTP printing plates
duty: Eliminate plate processor energy, water and chemistry in platemaking
trl_basis: Commercial product (Kodak Sonora) in widespread global use
key_constraints: Small absolute site energy saving (processors are minor loads); plate cost; run-length limits for some grades
uk_status: Widely used by UK newspaper and commercial printers
provenance: [kodak_processfree] Kodak publication on environmental benefits of process-free plates

option_name: Quarry solar PV (incl. floating PV on lagoons) with battery storage
duty: Onsite generation on quarry land/silt lagoons plus storage to supply plant and charge electric mobile plant at remote sites
trl_basis: 400kW floating solar array operational at a Cheshire quarry (E&T, June 2026)
key_constraints: Water-level variation in active lagoons; planning; storage sizing for plant start loads; restoration plans
uk_status: Operational UK example (Cheshire); ground-mount PV on quarry land increasingly common
provenance: [REF_EANDT26] UK quarry-specific floating solar deployment

option_name: Recycled cement paste as clinker (Cambridge Electric Cement / Cement 2 Zero)
duty: Reactivate hydrated cement from demolition waste as slag/clinker substitute in steel EAFs
trl_basis: No numeric TRL located; UKRI-funded Cement 2 Zero demonstration producing trial batches via Materials Processing Institute EAF
key_constraints: Coupled to EAF steelmaking capacity and slag chemistry; supply chain for demolition cement fines; early-stage scale-up; product standardisation
uk_status: UK-invented; Cement 2 Zero £6.5m industrial trial programme underway
provenance: [R_CEC] University of Cambridge cement recycling story; Cement 2 Zero project page (R_C2Z)

option_name: Refinery fuel switch to low-carbon (blue) hydrogen
duty: Fire refinery heaters, furnaces and boilers on low-carbon hydrogen from cluster supply
trl_basis: No published TRL; first hydrogen-ready furnace commissioned at Stanlow (2025), full H2 firing awaits EET HPP1 blue hydrogen plant (HyNet)
key_constraints: Dependent on HyNet H2 production/pipeline timing; burner and furnace conversion; NOx management
uk_status: UK-leading: EET Fuels Stanlow hydrogen-ready furnace operating on fuel gas; HPP1 government-backed
provenance: [eet_furnace_2025] EET Fuels announcement of hydrogen-ready furnace at Stanlow

option_name: Refinery process heater electrification
duty: Replace fired process heaters (crude, vacuum, reformer, hydrotreater feed) with electric resistance/impedance heaters
trl_basis: No formal published TRL located; small electric process heaters commercial, large radiant-duty e-heaters at concept/pilot stage per industry literature
key_constraints: Very large power demand and grid connection; loses refinery fuel gas sink; heater-by-heater replacement in turnarounds
uk_status: Studied in UK/EU refinery decarbonisation work; no UK deployment
provenance: [heater_elec_dt] Decarbonisation Technology article on electrification of process heaters

option_name: Rotating packed bed (HiGee) process intensification
duty: Intensified distillation/absorption/stripping in rotating packed beds cutting separation energy and footprint
trl_basis: No single published TRL; industrial applications reported for selected duties but HiGee distillation remains pilot-scale (Chem Eng Res Des industrial-application guide, 2018)
key_constraints: Rotating equipment maintenance; scale-up and column-replacement risk; strongly application-specific
uk_status: UK research base (e.g. Newcastle University); no known UK industrial retrofit
provenance: [rpb_guide_2018] Guide on industrial application of rotating packed beds

option_name: RotoDynamic electric heater for calciner/kiln process heat (Coolbrook)
duty: Turbomachinery-based electric heating of process air/material to >1000C (pathway to ~1700C), targeted at cement precalciners
trl_basis: No numeric TRL located; pilot testing completed 2023 exceeding 1000C; first industrial delivery to a cement producer announced 2026
key_constraints: Very large electrical demand and grid connection; kiln/calciner integration unproven; still leaves process CO2 (though in purer stream aiding capture)
uk_status: No UK deployment; pilot in Finland, first industrial cement deployment overseas
provenance: [R_COOLBROOK] Coolbrook pilot page: >1000C demonstrated, readiness for industrial-scale deployment

option_name: Shoe (extended-nip) press / advanced dewatering
duty: Mechanical dewatering upgrade raising post-press solids to cut paper machine drying steam demand
trl_basis: Long-established commercial technology widely installed since the 1990s (IPPTA design and applications review)
key_constraints: Requires press-section rebuild and machine downtime; benefit grade-dependent; high capex
uk_status: Widely deployed on UK machines at rebuilds; retrofit potential remains on older machines
provenance: [ippta_shoe_2012] IPPTA review of shoe press design and applications in paper machines

option_name: Shore power / cold ironing for berthed and docked vessels
duty: Grid electricity supply to vessels at berth/in dry dock so auxiliary diesel generators shut down during repair and outfitting
trl_basis: Commercially deployed at ports internationally; Energy Institute review of cold ironing status and barriers
key_constraints: High-capacity grid connection and frequency conversion; vessel-side compatibility; UK deployment lags and needs funding support
uk_status: Early UK deployments and government Green Maritime funding interest; British Ports Association pressing for support
provenance: [REF_COLDIRON] Energy Institute 'New Energy World' article on the case for cold ironing to cut port emissions

option_name: Solar thermal for industrial process heat (SHIP)
duty: Hot water/low-pressure heat: flat plate to ~100C, evacuated tube to ~120C, advanced designs 150-250C; concentrating collectors to ~400C
